items.title: UNICEF reports 172 children killed as Lebanon ceasefire takes effect

featured_image.name: The impact of conflict on Lebanon's children - UNICEF Australia

items.description: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect at midnight local time on April 17, offering a fragile pause in hostilities after 46 days of renewed war that has killed more than 2,100 people and displaced over one million. As the guns fell quiet, UNICEF reported that at least 172 children had been killed and 661 injured since fighting resumed on March 2, with more than 415,000 children forced from their homes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran denies agreeing to hand enriched uranium to US

featured_image.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran

items.description:
Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday flatly denied President Trump's assertion that Tehran had agreed to hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium to the United States, exposing a sharp public rift in fragile nuclear negotiations between the two countries.

"Iran's enriched uranium is not going to be transferred anywhere," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told state television. He added that the "transfer of Iran's enriched uranium to the US has never been raised in negotiations".[1][2][3]

The denial came hours after Trump told CBS News in a phone interview that Iran had "agreed to everything," including a joint operation to retrieve the country's roughly 2,000 kilograms of enriched uranium and bring it to American soil. "Our people, together with the Iranians, are going to work together to go get it. And then we'll take it to the United States," Trump said, adding that no U.S. troops would be involved.[4][5]

items.title: Trump says US has 'prohibited' Israel from bombing Lebanon

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Strait of Hormuz open ‘for remaining period of ceasefire’

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Friday that the United States has banned Israel from conducting further airstrikes in Lebanon, issuing his strongest public directive yet to constrain Israeli military operations as a fragile 10-day ceasefire between the two countries enters its first full day.

"Israel will not be bombing Lebanon any longer. They are PROHIBITED from doing so by the USA. Enough is enough," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The statement came as part of a broader post in which Trump also pushed back against Iran's efforts to link the Lebanon truce to ongoing U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations. "This deal is in no way subject to Lebanon, either, but the USA will, separately, work with Lebanon, and deal with the Hezboolah situation in an appropriate manner," he wrote.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says US will recover enriched uranium from Iran

featured_image.name: Trump holds situation room meeting on Iran nuclear deal ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States plans to work jointly with Iran to recover its stockpile of enriched uranium and transport it to the US, describing the effort as a gradual process that would begin soon.

"We're going to get it together. We're going to go in with Iran, at a nice leisurely pace, and go down and start excavating with big machinery… We'll bring it back to the United States," Trump told Reuters in a phone interview. He said what he called "nuclear dust" would be retrieved "very soon," referring to enriched uranium believed to remain underground after US and Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities at Fordow and Natanz in June 2025.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says Iran “agreed to everything” in war talks

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran has agreed to hand over enriched uranium

items.description: President Trump declared on Friday that Iran has "agreed to everything" in negotiations to end the weeks-long war between the two nations, claiming Tehran will surrender its enriched uranium stockpile and indefinitely suspend its nuclear program. Iran has not confirmed any such agreement.

items.title: Breeding top 1-5% of corals could boost reef survival, study finds

featured_image.name: Darwin in a lab: Coral evolution tweaked for global warming ...

items.description: A pair of studies published this week by an international team of coral scientists delivers both a warning and a roadmap: assisted evolution can help corals survive worsening marine heatwaves, but only if the research accelerates and selection is far more aggressive than anything tried so far.

items.title: Iran reopens Strait of Hormuz amid ceasefire as jet fuel crisis grips Europe

featured_image.name: Jet fuel shortage: Why Iran war could ground flights in Europe

items.description: Europe has roughly six weeks of jet fuel remaining, the head of the International Energy Agency warned on Thursday, raising the prospect of widespread flight cancellations just as the continent's peak summer travel season approaches. The warning came as the nearly seven-week closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke off a critical supply route for global energy.

items.title: Trump says Iran agreed to indefinitely suspend nuclear program; Tehran denies it

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes US is close to reaching a new Iran ...

items.description: President Donald Trump declared on Friday that Iran has agreed to suspend its nuclear program indefinitely, claiming a deal to end the war that has engulfed the Middle East since late February is "mostly complete." In a phone interview with Bloomberg, Trump said Tehran would not receive any frozen U.S. funds in exchange for the suspension and that talks toward a final agreement would likely resume over the weekend in Islamabad, Pakistan.[1][2]

items.title: Iran war reshapes global energy policy as nations fast-track renewables

featured_image.name: Iran war: A global energy shock could accelerate a shift to renewables

items.description:
The escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its seventh week — is reshaping global energy policy, as countries exposed to the largest oil supply disruption in decades accelerate their pivot toward renewable power.

Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil and gas supply transits, has locked an estimated 13 million barrels of oil per day out of global markets. A U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports, ordered by President Donald Trump on Monday after ceasefire talks collapsed, has further choked the waterway. The twin disruptions have pushed crude prices near historic highs and laid bare the vulnerabilities of fossil fuel dependency.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump keeps naval blockade despite Iran reopening Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump announces a Navy blockade in the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade on Iran will remain in place even after Tehran announced it was reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping, setting up a tense final stretch of negotiations before the ceasefire expires on April 22.

items.title: Oil plunges as Iran opens Strait of Hormuz to shipping

featured_image.name: Oil prices jump as shaky ceasefire keeps Strait of Hormuz in focus

items.description:
Oil prices tumbled sharply on Friday after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to all commercial vessels for the duration of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, sending crude to its lowest levels in five weeks and fueling a broad rally on Wall Street.

Brent crude fell roughly 10%, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate also dropped by double digits, according to CNN. The sell-off marked the steepest single-day decline since early April, when the initial U.S.-Iran ceasefire announcement sent prices plunging more than 15%.[1][2]

items.title: US delays weapons deliveries to European allies as Iran war strains stockpiles

featured_image.name: US delays arms supplies to EU amid operation in Iran — Reuters

items.description:
The United States has informed several European allies that previously contracted weapons deliveries will likely be delayed as the war with Iran continues to deplete American military stockpiles, Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing five sources familiar with the matter.[1][2]

Countries in the Baltic region and Scandinavia — some of which share a border with Russia — are among those affected, with delays hitting systems purchased under the Foreign Military Sales program that have not yet been delivered. U.S. officials communicated the expected postponements in bilateral messages to European counterparts in recent days, the sources said.[3][2][1]

items.title: Pope Leo XIV draws massive crowd at Douala Mass

featured_image.name: More than 500,000 expected at Pope Leo XIV's Mass in Cameroon

items.description:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before a crowd expected to number 600,000 at Japoma Stadium in Douala, Cameroon, on Friday, marking the largest gathering of his 11-day apostolic journey across Africa. The Vatican had predicted the turnout would be the biggest of the tour, though reports from the ground suggested attendance may have fallen short of projections due to extreme heat and tight security.[1][2]

The liturgy in Cameroon's economic capital came on the pontiff's third day in the country, part of a broader April 13–23 tour that began in Algeria and will continue to Angola and Equatorial Guinea. It is the first time an American pope has visited the African continent.[3][4]

items.title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open to all ships during ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iranian FM Araghchi says Strait of Hormuz remains open

items.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to all commercial vessels on Friday, linking the move to the 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon that took effect at midnight local time. The announcement marks the first time since the war began on February 28 that Tehran has offered unrestricted commercial passage through the waterway.

items.title: IATA warns Europe could see flight cancellations by late May amid jet fuel shortage

featured_image.name: Jet fuel shortage: Why Iran war could ground flights in Europe

items.description:
European flights could begin to be cancelled from the end of May due to dwindling jet fuel supplies, the International Air Transport Association warned on Friday, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke the continent's primary fuel supply route.[1][2]

IATA Director General Willie Walsh said the airline industry body's own estimates point to cancellations starting within weeks. "By the end of May we could start to see some cancellations in Europe for lack of jet fuel," Walsh said. The warning came a day after Fatih Birol, executive director of the International Energy Agency, told the Associated Press that Europe has "maybe six weeks or so of jet fuel left," calling the crisis "the largest energy crisis we have ever faced".[3][4][2]

items.title: NASA picks Falcon Heavy to launch ESA's Mars rover in 2028

featured_image.name: Watch Live as SpaceX's Falcon Heavy Rocket Launches Today ...

items.description:
NASA announced Thursday that it has approved the start of implementation for its contributions to the European Space Agency's long-delayed Rosalind Franklin Mars rover, selecting SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket to carry the mission to the Red Planet no earlier than late 2028.[1][2]

The approval moves the Rosalind Franklin Support and Augmentation (ROSA) project from the design phase into full implementation, a step that had been in question amid ongoing budget pressures from the Trump administration. The rover, if it launches on schedule, would arrive at Mars in 2030.[3][4][5]

items.title: European markets tread water ahead of weekend US-Iran talks

featured_image.name: European stocks finish in mixed territory amid volatile trading - CNBC

items.description: European stock markets traded in a narrow range on Friday as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of a potentially pivotal weekend of diplomacy between the United States and Iran. The pan-European STOXX 600 was subdued but on track to notch its fourth consecutive weekly gain, buoyed by lingering hopes that the conflict in the Middle East may be approaching a resolution.[1][2]

items.title: Kyushu researchers produce hydrogen from alcohol using iron and UV light

featured_image.name: Hydrogen made from alcohol by scientists using iron catalyst ...

items.description: Researchers at Kyushu University in Japan have discovered a remarkably simple method for producing hydrogen gas by combining iron ions with methanol and sodium hydroxide, then exposing the mixture to ultraviolet light. The findings, published in Communications Chemistry on April 17, represent a potential step toward cheaper and more sustainable hydrogen production.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says Iran deal is close as Lebanon ceasefire takes hold

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes US is close to reaching a new Iran ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump expressed confidence on Thursday that a deal to end the war with Iran is within reach, as a new 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon went into effect and diplomatic channels intensified ahead of a critical deadline next week.

"I think we're very close to making a deal with Iran," Trump told reporters outside the White House on Thursday. Speaking later in Las Vegas, he went further, saying the war "should be ending pretty soon". Trump indicated that a second round of in-person talks between the United States and Iran could take place as soon as this weekend in Islamabad, Pakistan, and said he might travel there himself if an agreement is signed.[1][2]

items.title: Thousands of displaced Lebanese head south as ceasefire takes hold

featured_image.name: Tens of thousands return to south Lebanon after ceasefire ...

items.description: Thousands of displaced Lebanese families surged onto highways heading south on Friday, hours after a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah took effect at midnight local time, halting weeks of devastating conflict that killed more than 2,100 people and uprooted over a million from their homes.[1][2]
